revision_rule.note: The 2012 rule creates automatic state bins only when a coverage point defines no bins; it does not extend that trigger to points containing only ignore_bins or illegal_bins, nor state the 2023 real-expression explicit-bin guarantee.

The 2017 rule creates automatic state bins only when no bins are defined at all, rather than also when the only definitions are ignore_bins or illegal_bins; 2017 also restricts coverpoints to integral expressions and therefore has no corresponding real-expression coverpoint rule.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no derived-covergroup inheritance or same-named coverpoint/cross override behavior.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no derived-covergroup inheritance or coverpoint/cross override semantics.
The 2017 covergroup grammar has the ordinary declaration form but lacks the `covergroup extends ...` alternative added to the current grammar.
IEEE 1800-2017 prohibits output and non-const ref arguments but does not state the current explicit prohibition on inout arguments.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no embedded covergroup extends declaration or covergroup inheritance construct.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no embedded covergroup extends declaration or covergroup inheritance construct.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no covergroup extends declaration form.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no covergroup extends declaration form.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no covergroup inheritance, including multilevel derived covergroups.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no covergroup inheritance construct.
IEEE 1800-2012 requires the specified coverpoint data type to be integral; it does not permit a real coverpoint type.
IEEE 1800-2017 requires a specified coverpoint type to be integral; it does not permit the current real type alternative.
IEEE 1800-2012 limits coverpoint expressions to integral expressions and has no real-expression sampled-value-bin or cross coverage.
IEEE 1800-2017 limits coverpoint expressions to integral types and has no real-expression coverpoint or real-bin/cross behavior.
The 2012 coverage-point grammar lacks the 2023 indexed covergroup value-range forms using +/- and +%-.
The 2017 coverage-point grammar lacks current real-range forms such as relative tolerance ranges, and its coverpoint semantics are integral-only.
The 2012 cross grammar lacks the 2023 indexed +/- and +%- value-range forms and the special `$` integer match-threshold alternative.
The 2017 cross grammar lacks current additions including `$` as a matches threshold and the newer relative-tolerance range forms.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no real-valued coverpoints or crosses of real-expression coverpoints.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no real-expression coverpoints, so neither direct real cross items nor crossed real-expression coverpoints are defined.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no cross_retain_auto_bins option or false-mode removal of all automatic cross bins.
IEEE 1800-2017 always retains nonintersecting automatic cross bins when user bins exist and has no cross_retain_auto_bins option to disable retention.
IEEE 1800-2012 retains nonoverlapping automatic cross bins alongside user bins, but has no cross_retain_auto_bins option to alter that behavior.
IEEE 1800-2017 defines coexistence and retention of nonintersecting automatic bins as fixed behavior; it has no cross_retain_auto_bins option controlling that behavior.
The 2012 definition-only restrictions cover per_instance, get_inst_coverage, auto_bin_max, and detect_overlap, but cross_retain_auto_bins does not exist.
IEEE 1800-2017 has the same definition-only restrictions for per_instance, get_inst_coverage, auto_bin_max, and detect_overlap, but has no cross_retain_auto_bins option.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no base and derived covergroup types.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no derived covergroup type or covergroup inheritance.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no derived covergroup argument inheritance.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no derived covergroup argument inheritance.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no derived covergroup component inheritance.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no covergroup inheritance of components.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no derived covergroup event inheritance.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no derived covergroup event inheritance.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no derived covergroup instance-replacement behavior.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no derived covergroup instance replacement semantics.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no derived covergroups that inherit or add coverage of base-class local properties.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no derived covergroup construct governing inherited coverage of base-local properties.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no derived covergroup option overriding.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no covergroup inheritance or derived option override behavior.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no derived covergroups or added derived coverpoints.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no derived covergroup coverpoint-addition behavior.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no derived coverpoint override contribution semantics.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no derived coverpoint override semantics.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no covergroup extends syntax.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no embedded covergroup extends syntax.
IEEE 1800-2012 supports discrete inclusive integral covergroup ranges but has no real-valued coverpoint ranges or continuous real interval semantics.
IEEE 1800-2017 defines integral covergroup ranges but has no real-expression coverpoints or real-bin range membership semantics.
The 2012 implicit option structures lack cross_retain_auto_bins and real_interval members that are present in the 2023 scope-specific compositions.
The 2017 implicit option structures lack the current cross_retain_auto_bins and real_interval members, so their exact member compositions differ.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no real-valued coverpoint bins or absolute-tolerance real ranges.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no real-expression coverpoint bins or absolute-tolerance bin range syntax.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no real-valued coverpoint bins to which a with filter could be applied.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no real-expression coverpoint bins and therefore no prohibition on with filtering for real bins.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no real-expression coverpoints or explicit-bin requirement for them.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not permit real-expression coverpoints.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no real-expression default bins.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no real-expression default bins.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no fixed bins for real coverpoint intervals.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no fixed-bin distribution semantics for real coverpoints.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no real fixed-bin interval distribution or excess-bin behavior.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no real fixed-bin arrays.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no real open-bin intervals or identical-interval merging.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no real open-bin intervals or interval-merging rule.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no real open-bin interval extents.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no real open-bin interval partition semantics.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no real open-bin interval naming rules.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no real open-array interval-bin naming rule.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no real coverpoint range partitioning or real_interval option.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no real coverpoint range partitioning or real_interval option.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no relative-tolerance real coverpoint ranges.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no relative-tolerance range syntax for real coverpoint bins.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no unbounded real coverpoint ranges.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no unbounded real covergroup range behavior.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no real coverpoint value-bin array forms.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no real coverpoint bin-array forms.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no real-type coverpoints or real wildcard-bin legality rule.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no real-type coverpoints or real wildcard-bin restriction.
The 2017 transition grammar supports the same repetition operators but lacks current covergroup range alternatives such as unbounded endpoints and tolerance-range forms.
IEEE 1800-2017 restricts all coverpoints to integral expressions, rather than permitting real coverpoints while specifically prohibiting only their transition bins.
IEEE 1800-2012 makes strobe definition-only but has no real_interval option; its other type options may be assigned procedurally.
IEEE 1800-2017 makes strobe definition-only and allows other type options procedurally, but has no real_interval type option.
IEEE 1800-2012 states that group-level type options do not default lower scopes and has no real_interval exception.
IEEE 1800-2017 states that group-level type options do not act as lower-level defaults and has no real_interval exception.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no real_interval type option or real-range bin partitioning.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no real_interval type option or real-bin interval partitioning.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no real_interval type option at any syntactic scope.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no real_interval type option and therefore no scope rule for it.
